proposed_widenings.name: permanent_feat_grant family
proposed_widenings.justification: Epic Boon grants a feat permanently at level-up. The only existing ClassFeatureMechanics family is 'activation', which requires activationCost + resource + resetCadence — all inapplicable to a permanent one-time character acquisition. No family exists for level-up progression grants.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see "Feats") or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_feat (ClassFeatureEffect variant)
proposed_widenings.justification: ClassFeatureEffect has no variant for feat acquisition. Existing variants are grant_extra_action and heal_hp, both of which are runtime effects of an activated feature. A feat grant is a permanent character ability acquisition during character progression, not a runtime activated effect.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see "Feats") or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

notes: This is a cross-class structural gap — every class has a Level 19 Epic Boon feature with this identical shape (barbarian, bard, cleric, druid, fighter, monk, paladin, ranger, rogue, sorcerer, warlock, wizard). The 'activation' family is fundamentally the wrong shape: it models repeatable activations with resource consumption and reset cadence. A feat grant at level-up is a one-time permanent acquisition during character progression — a categorically different concept. No ClassFeatureMechanics family currently covers permanent passive grants. No dhall or json authored; no trace produced.
